content.title: About
content.content: Haddock is a cold‑water marine fish of the cod family found in the North Atlantic. When baked or broiled, haddock offers tender white flesh, a mildly sweet flavor, and a lightly crisp crust when cooked properly.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Haddock is a key ingredient in the classic British dish “fish and chips”.
The flesh is high in protein but low in fat.
Haddock can change its skin coloration to blend with its surroundings, helping it avoid predators.
In the United States, haddock is one of the most commonly canned fish species.
Haddock can grow over 1 m in length, though most commercial catches are 30–50 cm.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Haddock contains very little saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as a powerful antioxidant protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides iodine
items.content: Iodine is necessary for normal thyroid gland activity.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to marine fish, including haddock.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: In certain regions haddock can accumulate mercury or cadmium; choose fish from reputable sources.

items.title: Nutrient loss with overcooking
items.content: Excessive high‑heat cooking can degrade heat‑sensitive vitamins such as B12.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Haddock can be baked with herbs, lemon, and olive oil or broiled until a golden crust forms. Serve with vegetable sides, mashed potatoes, or whole‑grain grains.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh haddock refrigerated at 0–2 °C and use within 2 days. Frozen fillets should be stored at –18 °C and consumed within 3–4 months. Rinse and pat dry before cooking.
